title: Crispy Garlic Beef
seoTitle: Sheet Pan Meatball Marinara Feed | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Oven-baked beef meatballs with marinara for ten
subtitle: Oven-baked beef meatballs with marinara for ten
description: Beef meatballs mix fast, bake on sheet pans until browned, then simmer in marinara until saucy. Serve over spaghetti or in sub rolls for a big crew feed that scales easy.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Garlic Beef in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Mix the meatballs
steps.instruction: Combine beef, breadcrumbs, eggs, Parmesan, garlic, salt, and pepper until just mixed. Roll into about 60 golf-ball-size meatballs.

steps.title: Bake on sheet pans
steps.instruction: Arrange meatballs on two parchment-lined sheet pans. Bake at 425°F 18–20 minutes until browned and internal temp reaches 160°F. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Simmer in marinara
steps.instruction: Transfer meatballs to large pots, cover with marinara, and simmer 15 minutes until sauce coats meatballs and centers reach 165°F. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Boil spaghetti
steps.instruction: Cook spaghetti in salted water until al dente while meatballs simmer. Drain and toss with a ladle of sauce. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crispy Garlic Beef onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 10 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Serve the spread
steps.instruction: Serve meatballs and sauce over spaghetti with basil. Toast sub rolls with mozzarella for meatball subs on the same line. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Bake a test meatball first if you are unsure on seasoning—adjust mix before rolling all 60.
Italian seasoning tablespoon in the mix saves chopping extra herbs.
Meatballs freeze raw on sheet pans—transfer to bags for emergency feeds.
tonightSpread: Spaghetti and meatballs with garlic bread and extra Parmesan.
Meatball subs with melted mozzarella for handheld eaters.
leftovers: Meatball parm bake: layer in dish with mozzarella and bake 375°F.
Crush into pizza topping for a quick flatbread night.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Meatballs feed a crowd without carving or portion guesswork. Sheet pan bake beats standing at a skillet forming batches, and subs plus pasta covers different appetites.
mealPrepNotes: Use a scoop for uniform meatballs—they bake evenly. Bake at high heat for color, then finish in sauce. Spaghetti can boil while meatballs bake.
